title: Reduce console backend noise and optimize aggregation pathways
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Over the last 6 months the Console backend aggregator layer has accumulated ad-hoc feature patches: multiple per-route GraphQL resolvers that fan out to the same downstream services, inconsistent cache key schemes, and a legacy batching layer that times out too conservatively. These contribute to elevated 99th percentile tail latency and noisy CPU usage during bursts.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end tail latency for the Console 'Overview' and 'Routes' screens by 30% and lower aggregate CPU spikes by simplifying the aggregation pipeline and standardizing cache semantics. Deliver a low-risk, incremental rollout with observability and automatic fallback.

Scope:
- Replace the highest-impact request paths' custom fanout logic with a shared aggregation service (in-process to start; plan for extraction later).
- Standardize cache key derivation across GraphQL resolvers and the REST aggregation endpoints. Migrate from per-field in-memory caches to a single sharded LRU with TTLs tuned by route.
- Rework resolver batching: move from heuristic-driven batching windows to workload-aware continuous batching with a minimum batch size and backpressure signals to avoid excessive small batches.
- Remove redundant GraphQL selection merging steps that cause double deserialization on hot paths.
- Upgrade two soft dependencies: graphql-js -> 17.5.0 and node-lru-cache -> 8.1.3 to pick up improved eviction and metrics hooks.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Decrease p99 latency for Overview and Routes API paths by >= 30% in staging and canary.
- Reduce median and p95 CPU consumption during synthetic burst tests by >= 15%.
- No increase in error rate or user-facing partial responses.
- Migration can be rolled back through a single feature flag toggle per service.

Implementation plan (phased):
Phase A (this ticket):
- Add shared aggregation helper module and feature-flagged wiring in console-backend.
- Introduce unified cache key util and migrate 2 critical resolvers.
- Add metrics for batch sizes, cache hit/miss, serialization time.
- Run canary traffic (5% production) with aggressive tracing.
Phase B (follow-up ticket):
- Complete resolver migrations, tune TTLs by route using traffic replay.
- Extract aggregation helper into standalone microservice if measurable CPU cross-talk remains.
Phase C (polish):
- Dependency upgrades on remaining services, add e2e performance tests to CI.

Testing and validation:
- Local and staging unit tests for cache key determinism and eviction correctness.
- Synthetic load tests (k6) that replicate 95th/99th tail behavior using production traces.
- Canary with traffic mirroring for 48h, with automatic rollback on error thresholds.

Rollback strategy:
- Feature flags per binary to revert shared aggregation and fallback to original fanout logic instantly.
- Backfill cache warm-up via traffic replay to eliminate cold-start penalty if rollback occurs mid-migration.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Inconsistent cache semantics causing subtle stale reads. Mitigation: conservative TTLs and route-level cache-busting in rollout.
- Risk: Semantic drift from resolver consolidation. Mitigation: automated snapshot tests comparing JSON responses against baseline for a representative prompt set.
- Risk: Dependency upgrade surface area. Mitigation: lockfile isolate and smoke-testing harness in CI.

Observability changes required:
- New histograms for per-aggregation-step latency.
- Batch-size distribution gauge and continuous batch fill ratio.
- Cache hit/miss per route.
- Console dashboard tile and alert: p99 > 300ms on Overview route for 10m -> page oncall.

Notes: this ticket focuses on engineering debt removal with minimal product changes. UX is unaffected; coordination with product/design is minimal but we will add a PM review step before canary if rollout affects response shape.

2026-02-24 - Rahul Shah: Spike completed — implementing shared aggregation helper reduced duplicated serialization by ~40% in local profiling. Initial patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4823

2026-03-02 - SRE (Priya Patel): Reviewed rollout plan. Added requirements for a canary pipeline and indicated 5% traffic mirror is available on canary cluster. Also requested an alert on batch fill ratio dropping below 20%.

2026-03-05 - Rahul Shah: Implemented unified cache-key util and migrated RoutesResolver to new scheme. Added metrics: console.agg.batch_size, console.cache.hit_ratio by route. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4857

2026-03-08 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Running staging load tests. Initial results: p99 reduced by 18% (still short of target). Observed some small increase in p50 due to serialization consolidation; investigating micro-optimizations.
2026-03-10 - Rahul Shah: Tuned batching parameters (minBatch=4, maxWindowMs=12) which cut p99 further during synthetic bursts. Preparing canary rollout for 2026-03-12.
2026-03-12 - Rollout: Canary (5%) started. Initial metrics report: Overview p99 down 29% in canary, CPU spike frequency down ~20%. Monitoring for 24h before ramping.
